image_description: A close-up, top-down view of a lionfish (Pterois) resting on a textured, rocky seabed. The fish displays characteristic red and white vertical stripes on its body. Its most prominent features are the long, needle-like dorsal spines fanning out from its back and the large, fan-shaped pectoral fins with elongated rays extending to the sides. The head is visible with a dark eye, and the pelvic fins are partially visible beneath the body. There is a watermark text in the bottom right corner.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Laterally compressed body with moderately sized proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body appears laterally compressed (tall and thin from side view, though seen from top-down, the height is evident). Proportions match standard lionfish morphology.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Brightly striped coloration in red, white, brown, or black bands.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Distinct vertical reddish-brown and white bands are clearly visible along the flanks of the fish.

While lionfish have small scales, the resolution and lighting of this specific image make it impossible to definitively resolve individual scales versus general skin texture. Marking as untestable to avoid false negative on texture.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large fan-like pectoral fins with elongated rays.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Pelvic fins also with elongated spines.
